A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COMPASS framework and Comp-11 dataset. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original composition-perception and generation experiments, component ablations, qualitative results and KU-PCP classification results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds independent-proxy evaluation, UNIAA out-of-distribution results and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The C-MoE architecture, expert token, grayscale pixelization, attention mask, cross-attention refinement and two-stage training remain unchanged. PhotoFramer is introduced for evaluation, without modifying the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds zero-shot perception and generation evaluation on UNIAA beyond the retained Comp-11 and KU-PCP coverage. Figure 10 also introduces cross-domain generation examples involving everyday photographs and watercolors, substantially extending the tested input domains.

E2.justification: PhotoFramer, previously only discussed as related work, becomes an evaluated perception comparator in v2 Table 8. The existing perception baselines are retained, and generation comparisons still use Step1X-Edit, BAGEL and Ming-Lite-Uni.

E3.justification: v2 adds PhotoFramer-based composition scoring alongside the retained COMPASS-based evaluation. It also introduces a zero-shot UNIAA protocol with 1,424 perception samples balanced by category and 354 generation pairs. Original training settings remain unchanged; uniform coverage of the 10,000 Comp-11 generation pairs was already specified in v1.

E4.justification: New analyses test cross-dataset generalization, dependence on the model's own composition evaluator, and cross-domain disentanglement. Figure 10 adds a semantic-layout conflict failure case. Existing component ablations and the pixelization-only BAGEL analysis are retained, including v1 Figure 11 becoming v2 Figure 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged. New Tables 6 and 8 report substantial additional results, including COMPASS proxy composition consistency of 0.71 in-domain and 0.77 OOD, and reported OOD mAP of 89.2 versus PhotoFramer's 76.2. Appendix B.4 adds 3.25s versus 3.38s latency measurements. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15, mathematical definitions and objective formulations are retained, with no new theorem, proof or derivation. Using PhotoFramer changes the evaluation procedure without introducing a revised mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified composition perception and generation, the Comp-11 dataset, a shared expert-token anchor and generation without paired layout-transfer training images.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges circular self-evaluation and explains why composition consistency should be interpreted jointly with text alignment. It interprets OOD results as generalized disentanglement and adds physical realism versus layout adherence as a failure mechanism, while shortening the earlier directional-error diagnosis. New Appendix E additionally asserts applicability to lighting, emotional tone and camera movement without corresponding experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly documents approximately 8B added parameters, 22% static VRAM overhead and single-A100 timing. v2 also supplies a PhotoFramer evaluator link and expands release claims to trained models and metric scripts. Table 5's implementation settings are unchanged, and release availability remains inconsistently described as current versus future.

R1.justification: The reference list and Related Work section are unchanged. The appendix newly positions PhotoFramer as an independent evaluator and comparator, contrasts UNIAA's coverage with Comp-11, and expands the framework's positioning toward general abstract visual control.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized appendix additions and rewrites, new computational-cost and OOD subsections, a Broader Impact section, and revised failure and privacy discussion. Affiliations and corresponding-author information also change. The main scientific narrative is retained without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 8 and the OOD montage in Figure 10. Figure 1 moves from the title page to page 2; the original KU-PCP table and later figures are relocated or renumbered. Existing visual content and the overall presentation style are retained.

improvement.justification: The added third-party scoring and UNIAA tests strengthen evidence beyond v1's self-evaluated generation results, while computational-cost disclosure and a new failure case improve transparency. However, PhotoFramer adaptation and similarity-feature extraction remain underspecified, and Appendix E extends applicability claims beyond the tested tasks. These limitations temper the otherwise useful evidence and documentation gains.
